items.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: if you drove by and saw a billboard with the Count Basie band instead of Ricky Martin or something.

ctx.x: And I don’t know how to educate audiences to, you know, you must like this new kind of harmony, or that kind of thing, like to get people to like that. Because the diversity between a festival like this and some of the — well now you can’t even really count some of the festivals as jazz festivals because the headliners will be James Brown and Earth Wind & Fire, things that have nothing to do with jazz at all but they’ve become just big music festivals just to keep the crowd interested. And again it’s a whole…
Well you know jazz I think takes some work to listen to. I think it’s not as easily accessible to peoples’ ears somehow. A lot of people don’t understand — oh I like jazz © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-
